correctness.rationale: For the deterministic map with b=beta−1 and balanced sources, the log-odds drift is (b−1)P−bQ. On the right of the midpoint, P/Q increases strictly from 3 to infinity because it is the Q'-weighted mean of the strictly increasing derivative ratio (1+2/[x(1−x)])/3. The signs, including b=1 and b=3/2, yield precisely the fixed points, and strict monotonicity of the map prevents crossing them, so monotone convergence gives the claimed basins. At b=3/2 the log-odds drift is (64/27)u^3+O(u^5), giving (16/27)u^3 after applying the logistic map. Independent symbolic expansion corroborated this and K(1/2+u)=3+(32/9)u^2+O(u^4); the root level is 3+4(3/2−b)+O((3/2−b)^2), which gives the stated collision coefficient and remainder. Small asymmetry adds a constant log[p/(1−p)] to the interior equation, preserving the three simple roots locally. Compact complements exclude extra interior roots, while uniform O(x^b) endpoint bounds for b>1 exclude extra roots near 0 and 1. The endpoint fixed points themselves persist exactly. Frozen RESULT.md §§1–5, VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were inspected; the supplied verifier was not run. The conclusion concerns neither finite random source batches nor arbitrary p away from 1/2.

value.rationale: The binary distribution is a natural, analytically tractable test of the existing normalized preference model. Its three distinct attraction basins in the intermediate regime show that extreme-versus-consensus is not an exhaustive dichotomy. Sharp boundaries, exact separatrices up to one monotone equation, and the perturbation result distinguish robust multistability from a balance-only degeneracy. The value is mathematical within the deterministic model, not a social prediction.
